novelty_flags.label: oeq:adaptive-linearization and thm:joint-cfse
novelty_flags.one_line: Add Berthier–Montanari–Nguyen (2020) on non-separable AMP state evolution and Javanmard–Montanari (2013) on general AMP state evolution as close structural comparators before maintaining the claim that available AMP theory is exhausted.

soundness_flags.label: def:moment-vector, def:cfse, oeq:adaptive-linearization, thm:joint-cfse
soundness_flags.one_line: The recursion and derivative are defined only for P in the exact fixed-rank domain and tangent directions preserving deleted pivots, but M_N and I_T use the unconstrained empirical law P_N and point-mass directions delta_xi-P_xi without a condition that they remain in that domain; at a deleted pivot this is precisely the nonregular |delta| phenomenon the diagnostic exhibits.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:joint-cfse and thm:path-bands
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Accepted conditionally only for fixed T, Gaussian homogeneous interactions, independent initial rows and assignments, and the deterministic population-limit estimand rather than a realized finite-network counterfactual.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The claimed root-N law and bands are conditional results for the stated homogeneous Gaussian Causal-MP model and its population-limit path.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper establishes exponential finite-sample concentration around AMP state evolution for i.i.d. Gaussian measurement matrices, rather than a causal empirical root-N covariance expansion.

The published article gives a nonasymptotic leave-one-out representation for AMP iterates under broad Gaussian random-matrix models and distinguishes it from ordinary low-dimensional empirical state evolution.
The paper generalizes Gaussian-matrix AMP state evolution to Lipschitz non-separable nonlinearities using conditioning and Long AMP; it is a close first-order comparator omitted from the core.
The paper establishes state evolution for a general AMP class with independent, non-identically distributed Gaussian entries; it is another close first-order comparator omitted from the core.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Repair the deleted-pivot regime before solving: either restrict the headline theorem to the all-active interior where the empirical law remains in an open rank-stable neighborhood, or define a rank-preserving statistic/model identity and prove that its empirical perturbations stay on the zero-pivot stratum.

Add Berthier–Montanari–Nguyen (2020) and Javanmard–Montanari (2013), explicitly state why their first-order AMP theorems do not supply the proposed aggregate fluctuation law, and correct the Bao–Han–Xu pagination to 2716–2766.

After the regularity repair, sharpen the contribution around a directly estimable common-disorder covariance component and compare its band width or coverage against the published Causal-MP resampling heuristic on the affine witness and a generic non-affine class.
